question.text: Suppose that the points <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> lie on the line <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> If a line <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> passing through the points <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is perpendicular to <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> then <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> equals:

solution.text:
Slope of line L1 is 4-2-3-1=2-4=-12
Hence slope of L2 is 2.
From line L1,  k-2h-1=-12
⇒h+2k=5 …..(1)
From line L2,  k-3h-4=2
⇒k=2h-5 ..…(2)
From (1) and (2) h=3 and k=1
⇒kh=13
